title: The First Pigment laser Omakase
intro: A first visit for uneven tone and scattered brown marks that combines Enlighten Pico toning, Clarity Pro for the skin surface, and a targeted laser for individual spots, together with a physician consultation. The physician may adjust or hold back the laser after examining your skin.
questions: Which of my marks are surface spots, and do any look like melasma that needs a gentler plan?
Would my skin tone or recent sun exposure change or postpone any part of the laser today?
How might treated spots look while I am still travelling, and whom do I contact if a reaction worsens at home?

sections.title: What is checked before any laser
sections.text: The physician looks at the type and spread of pigment, your skin tone and any recent tanning. A deep tan, an active acne flare or rash, pregnancy or breastfeeding can each defer the laser. Darker skin may be treated with adjusted settings, or the targeted step changed or postponed.

sections.title: What one visit can and cannot do
sections.text: This is designed as a low-commitment introduction, not a course. Visible change and its timing vary, and pigment is not promised to clear. Melasma tends to be managed over time rather than removed, so it may need a different plan than this visit offers.

sections.title: Other starting points
sections.text: If the pigment appears deeper or more widespread, the separate Enlighten pigment treatment may fit better. If breakouts keep leaving new marks, acne control may come first. The consultation can also cover lifting, filler or skin quality, with no obligation to book anything more.

sections.title: Recovery and travel
sections.text: Redness, warmth and sensitivity are common, and treated spots can darken or crust lightly for a while. Whether you can fly the same day is decided after the physician sees how your skin responded; an itinerary is not medical clearance. Written aftercare is provided.

title: The Body Filler Omakase
intro: Non-surgical soft-volume filler for the shoulder line, with hip treatment considered after in-person assessment. It is intended for people at a stable weight whose proportions have not changed with training. The physician maps the area photographically and starts conservatively.
questions: Is the gap in my shoulder or hip line something filler can address, or would surgery or fat transfer suit it better?
Which body-grade product is planned, and can it be dissolved if I am unhappy with the result?
When can I return to training that loads the treated area, and is my stay long enough for the follow-up review?

sections.title: How suitability is judged
sections.text: Measurement and photographic mapping decide where volume goes, rather than simply where you point. The physician considers weight stability, your training routine and how much change you want. Front, back and angled photos in fitted sportswear help the clinic say beforehand whether a consultation is worth the trip.

sections.title: Honest limits
sections.text: Filler is temporary and is broken down by the body at a rate that varies with activity, body region and product. It is not suited to a large change in volume; in that case a surgical referral is the honest answer. Whether a product can be reversed depends on which one is used.

sections.title: Alternatives
sections.text: Implants are surgical, and fat transfer moves your own fat; both are different decisions with different recovery. Where the concern is loose skin or a small pocket of fat rather than a missing curve, body radiofrequency or a fat-dissolving injection may be discussed instead.

sections.title: Recovery, training and travel
sections.text: Swelling and bruising vary by person. Walking and light activity are usually fine soon after, while heavy training that loads the area pauses for a period the physician confirms. A follow-up is normally planned some weeks later, so check how that fits your travel.

title: Tune Eye Cell
intro: An under-eye treatment using Lafullen, a polycaprolactone-based collagen-stimulating injectable, placed in layers the physician chooses after examining shadow, hollowing, skin thickness and wrinkle depth. It aims at gradual support rather than immediate filling.
questions: Is my under-eye darkness actually a volume problem, or is it puffiness, pigment or loose eyelid skin?
How does a collagen stimulator differ from hyaluronic-acid filler in my case, including what happens if I dislike the result?
How much bruising might still show on my flight home, and should I schedule treatment earlier in my trip?

sections.title: Is it a volume problem?
sections.text: Not every dark under-eye is caused by hollowing. Puffy bags, brown pigment in the skin and loose eyelid skin have different causes, and an injectable may not help them. The physician assesses this first and says plainly when another approach is worth considering.

sections.title: What to expect from the product
sections.text: Polycaprolactone particles are placed in the deeper layer, where the intended action is to support collagen formation over time. Change develops gradually and is reviewed at follow-up. How much changes, and when, varies by individual and is not predicted in advance; smoothness cannot be guaranteed.

sections.title: Alternatives
sections.text: Where skin quality rather than hollowing is the main concern, polynucleotide or PDRN injections, or a PDLLA stimulator such as Juvelook, may be discussed. Previous under-eye filler, eyelid surgery or other treatment in the area should be mentioned because it affects the plan.

sections.title: Bruising and travel timing
sections.text: The under-eye bruises and swells easily, and swelling, bruising or unevenness can occur. Numbing and cooling help comfort but do not remove these risks. Send your flight date before booking and be prepared for some bruising to remain visible on the way home.

title: Acne Care Package
intro: An acne program built from photodynamic therapy (PDT) and gold photothermal therapy (Gold PTT), both aimed at the sebaceous glands and inflammation rather than surface soothing alone. The physician grades your acne in person before choosing one, the other or both.
questions: What severity stage is my acne, and how many sessions can realistically fit within my stay?
Does my current acne medication or skincare change whether PDT or Gold PTT is appropriate?
How long must I avoid strong light after PDT, and how does that affect sightseeing and my flight?

sections.title: What the physician grades
sections.text: The assessment covers acne severity, skin type and the medication and skincare you use now. From that, the physician sets which treatment to use, the order and the number of sessions by severity stage, rather than applying a fixed package. Extraction is added where appropriate.

sections.title: Control, not cure
sections.text: Acne involves sebum, blocked follicles, bacteria, inflammation and hormones, so treatment is usually about control. Recurrence can still happen. Neither PDT nor Gold PTT is presented as preventing acne from returning or avoiding scarring, and the combination is not claimed to outperform either alone.

sections.title: Related options
sections.text: Once breakouts are under control, marks left behind may be considered with pigment laser, and textural scars through staged scar revision or radiofrequency microneedling. Scar work usually waits until active acne settles, so the order of treatment matters.

sections.title: Recovery and light after PDT
sections.text: Redness, dryness, peeling or a temporary flare before improvement can occur. After PDT you avoid strong light for a period the physician sets, which matters for outdoor plans and daytime travel. Leave a buffer before flights and events and confirm it at consultation.

title: TenTherma Lifting
intro: TenTherma is a monopolar radiofrequency device that heats the dermis, with collagen remodelling over the following months as the intended effect. A range of tip sizes lets the physician match energy delivery to each zone of the face, neck or body.
questions: Is my loss of firmness mainly in the skin, or does deeper sagging mean another approach would suit me better?
Which areas and tip sizes would you plan, and is a single visit reasonable for my trip?
Do any of my implants, devices or recent treatments rule this out or change the timing?

sections.title: Who it is assessed for
sections.text: The consultation focuses on loss of firmness and crepey texture on the face, eye area, neck or body. Tell the clinic which area you mean, since the plan follows the area. Recent lifting or laser treatments and your travel dates help the physician propose a realistic first plan.

sections.title: What it does not claim
sections.text: The clinic does not claim TenTherma reaches deeper than other radiofrequency devices or acts on the SMAS layer. Choosing a tip is part of planning, not a guarantee. The small study cited by Tune Clinic concerns monopolar radiofrequency as a class and does not establish results for TenTherma.

sections.title: When something else fits
sections.text: If most of the sagging comes from deeper tissue, focused ultrasound such as Ultherapy, or a thread lift, may be discussed. Thermage and Oligio are other monopolar radiofrequency options; the choice between devices is made at assessment rather than by name.

sections.title: Safety screening and recovery
sections.text: Mention a pacemaker or implanted electrical device, metal implants in the area, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Active dermatitis, acne flares or infection are assessed first. Flushing, warmth, mild swelling, tenderness or dryness can follow, so flag any event or flight close to the date.

title: InMode for the Body
intro: Radiofrequency heat delivered beneath the skin while a suction handpiece holds the tissue, used to address the look of cellulite and loose skin on the abdomen, flanks, thighs, upper arms and back. It is not a weight-loss treatment.
questions: In my area, is the issue mostly loose skin, fat or cellulite, and does that make this device a sensible choice?
Would one visit be meaningful, or is a course needed that my time in Seoul cannot cover?
How likely is bruising from the suction, and will it affect what I wear or do on my trip?

sections.title: How the area is assessed
sections.text: The physician examines the area for skin looseness and the amount of fat present, then marks where energy will go. A tip module and settings are chosen for that area. If another option fits the area better, the physician says so rather than proceeding.

sections.title: Realistic expectations
sections.text: How much the look of cellulite or skin firmness changes differs between people, and it does not replace weight loss. Suction is how the device is applied, not an established added benefit. Temperature monitoring is a control measure, not a promise of a painless or risk-free session.

sections.title: Alternatives
sections.text: For a missing curve rather than loose skin, body filler may be discussed. A small, defined pocket of fat may suit a fat-dissolving injection, and other energy devices such as Onda target fat and laxity differently. The choice follows the examination.

sections.title: Screening, recovery and course length
sections.text: Tell the physician about pregnancy, a pacemaker, metal implants in the area, or broken or inflamed skin there. Heat and pulling are expected; redness, warmth, tenderness and bruising can follow. Some plans are one visit and some are a course, so share how long you are staying.

title: Ultherapy
intro: Ultherapy places focused ultrasound heat at set depths beneath the skin, including the SMAS layer, without an incision. Any change comes from collagen remodelling, so it builds gradually and varies. The physician sets the shot count and placement after examining you.
questions: Where does my looseness actually sit, and would Thermage, both, or neither suit it better than Ultherapy?
Why is the shot count you recommend the right dose for my anatomy rather than a larger tier?
Is same-day flying reasonable for me given tenderness, my medical history and the length of my flight?

sections.title: Who it is assessed for
sections.text: The usual consultation focus is early looseness along the jawline, lower face and under the chin. The physician marks lines and depths on your face before any energy is used. Daylight photos and a note of previous lifting, filler or threads help shape a first answer before you travel.

sections.title: Limits worth knowing
sections.text: Marked excess skin, a very lean face or active infection may point to a different plan. More shots do not add lift if energy goes into the wrong plane. Change is expected to develop gradually. The small study cited by Tune Clinic cannot predict your result or how long any change will last.

sections.title: How it compares
sections.text: Thermage warms a broad area of the dermis with radiofrequency, while Ultherapy targets set depths with ultrasound; neither is a stronger version of the other. Some faces suit one, some both, some neither. Other focused ultrasound devices on the menu include Shurink and CoolSoniq.

sections.title: Comfort, recovery and flights
sections.text: Most people feel each pulse as a deep ache or hot prickle, often strongest over bone. Numbing is discussed and you can ask for a pause. Redness, swelling or tenderness along the jaw can occur. Send your itinerary before booking so flying home can be considered.

title: Thermage
intro: Thermage heats the deep dermis with monopolar radiofrequency through a cooled, vibrating tip, for early looseness on the jawline, cheeks and around the eyes. Some firmness may be felt soon after, but most change depends on collagen remodelling over months.
questions: Is my laxity early enough for a dermal treatment, or is the sagging too heavy for Thermage to address?
Which areas, including the eye area, would you treat, and how would that change my time in clinic?
Do my implants, medical devices or skin condition rule Thermage out or change the plan?

sections.title: What the assessment looks for
sections.text: The physician examines where the looseness sits on the jawline, cheeks and eye area, then decides the areas and shot count. Photos from the front and both sides, earlier lifting, filler or threads with rough dates, and any implants help decide whether planning around your trip makes sense.

sections.title: What it is not designed for
sections.text: Thermage is not designed for heavy sagging or a large amount of excess skin. How much change you see and how long it lasts vary, so any repeat is planned at follow-up rather than fixed. The small comparison study cited by Tune Clinic does not establish results for a specific Thermage generation.

sections.title: Comparable options
sections.text: Ultherapy delivers focused ultrasound to set depths including the SMAS, while Thermage warms a broad dermal area. Oligio and TenTherma are other monopolar radiofrequency devices. A thread lift may be discussed when tissue needs repositioning. The examination, not the price, guides the choice.

sections.title: Screening and recovery
sections.text: A pacemaker or implanted electrical device, metal implants in the area, active skin infection, pregnancy or breastfeeding can rule it out. Each pulse feels hot despite cooling, and you can ask for pauses. Redness, warmth, swelling or tenderness can follow, so mention any event or flight nearby.

title: Thread Lifting
intro: Absorbable threads are placed under the skin, under anesthesia, to reposition sagging tissue in the cheeks, jawline or under the chin. Collagen forming around the threads is the intended second effect. The physician may also conclude that threads are not right for you.
questions: How do my anatomy and skin thickness affect which thread type, number and direction you would use?
How many days should I allow in Seoul before flying, given the threads planned for me?
What would a visible or palpable thread, dimpling or asymmetry mean, and how is it handled once I am home?

sections.title: Deciding whether threads fit
sections.text: The physician examines sagging in the mid-face, jawline and under the chin and marks the vectors the threads will follow. Very heavy skin excess, active skin infection or a recent procedure in the same area can make threads unsuitable. Blood thinners and supplements should be mentioned beforehand.

sections.title: How long it holds
sections.text: The threads are absorbed over time. How much change holds, and for how long, depends on the person, skin, thread choice and technique, and cannot be promised. Thread lifting repositions tissue; where the issue is lost volume, threads alone may not address it.

sections.title: Alternatives to discuss
sections.text: For early looseness without much descent, energy devices such as Ultherapy, Thermage or Shurink are non-invasive options. Where cheeks look hollow at the sides, Cheek Hollow Lifting applies threads to that pattern, and true volume loss may need a separate volume treatment.

sections.title: Downtime and travel
sections.text: Swelling, bruising, tightness or a pulling feeling can follow, and wide yawning or hard chewing may aggravate it early on. Scheduling the procedure early in your trip lets any problem be seen before you leave. Share arrival and departure dates first.

title: Shurink Lifting
intro: Shurink is a HIFU device that focuses ultrasound into small points of heat in the upper dermis, lower dermis and SMAS layer. Sessions are short, and the physician sets depth and settings after examining you. Collagen remodelling is the intended effect.
questions: Is my lower-face looseness early enough for HIFU, or would heavier sagging need a different plan?
How would you decide whether repeat sessions or maintenance make sense for me?
How much tenderness along the jaw should I expect, and will it affect my plans in the following days?

sections.title: What is assessed
sections.text: The usual focus is a softening jawline and early looseness in the lower face. The physician decides depth, settings and shot count after looking at your skin and what you want to change. Previous lifting, filler or threads in the lower face should be mentioned with rough dates.

sections.title: Limitations
sections.text: Heavy sagging or a lot of loose skin usually needs a different plan, and a very lean face is a reason to pause. There is no fixed course; the number of sessions and any maintenance are decided in person and reviewed. How much changes, and for how long, varies.

sections.title: Comparable approaches
sections.text: Ultherapy and CoolSoniq also use focused ultrasound at set depths. Radiofrequency options such as Oligio heat the dermis instead. Potenza addresses texture and pores rather than lift. The physician explains which tool fits the layer where your change sits.

sections.title: Comfort and recovery
sections.text: Most people feel prickling or warmth, often stronger over bone along the jaw; numbing cream can reduce it and you can ask for pauses. Redness, warmth, tenderness or mild swelling can occur. Active acne or infection in the area, pregnancy or breastfeeding are reasons to wait.

title: Rejuran
intro: Rejuran is a salmon-derived polynucleotide injectable used for skin quality, such as thin, dry or finely lined skin. It does not add volume or change contour. The physician confirms the product, area and number of sessions after examining your skin.
questions: Is my concern skin quality that Rejuran targets, or is it volume loss that it will not change?
If I can only come once, how would the plan differ from a series of sessions?
How long might injection bumps stay visible before photos, meetings or my flight?

sections.title: What the physician considers
sections.text: The assessment looks at skin quality, texture and fine lines. Daylight photos without makeup, recent boosters, filler or laser, and your travel dates help the physician suggest which option to discuss. A fish or salmon allergy, active skin infection, pregnancy or breastfeeding must be raised first.

sections.title: What it will not do
sections.text: Rejuran is for skin quality, not contour, so it is the wrong tool for hollows or sagging. There is no fixed course; sessions and spacing depend on your skin and goals. How much changes, and for how long, varies and is reviewed as your skin responds.

sections.title: Related injectables
sections.text: Products sold as polynucleotide and as PDRN are not interchangeable, and the physician tells you which formulation is used. Juvelook and the Tune Re2O collagen boosters aim at collagen stimulation. Hydration boosters mainly draw water into the skin, and filler adds volume.

sections.title: Comfort and visible marks
sections.text: It is a series of small injections after numbing cream, and areas such as under the eyes can feel more sensitive. Small bumps, redness or bruising can appear at injection points. Share event and travel dates so the plan leaves enough time.

title: Juvelook
intro: Juvelook is an injectable PDLLA collagen stimulator used in two ways: finely diluted and placed shallow as a skin booster, or prepared thicker and placed deeper for soft volume. The physician chooses the approach, or a mix, and the amount at consultation.
questions: For my concern, would the skin approach, the volume approach or a mix make more sense, and why?
How will I tell early swelling apart from real change in the weeks after treatment?
How much buffer should I leave before events or flights for bumps or bruising to settle?

sections.title: Choosing the approach
sections.text: The physician looks at skin texture, pores, fine lines and areas that have lost soft volume, along with your facial structure. The skin approach spreads a fine preparation across an area, while the volume approach places a thicker preparation in chosen spots. The amount is explained before treatment.

sections.title: Timing and limits
sections.text: Change is not immediate. Collagen stimulation develops gradually, and how much develops, and over what period, varies and is reviewed at follow-up. Early swelling can resemble volume and then settle, which is expected. Pregnancy, breastfeeding or active infection in the area are reasons not to treat.

sections.title: Alternatives
sections.text: Rejuran targets skin quality through a polynucleotide rather than a collagen stimulator, and Tune Re2O is another collagen booster family. Radiesse offers structural support with calcium hydroxylapatite. The physician compares these against your goal.

sections.title: Recovery while travelling
sections.text: Swelling, small bumps, redness or bruising can appear at injection points, and how long they stay visible varies. Send daylight photos, the area that concerns you and your dates in Seoul so the plan leaves a sensible buffer.

title: Botox
intro: A physician-led botulinum toxin injection for facial expression lines, a square jaw from an enlarged masseter muscle, and the shoulder and calf lines. Which areas suit you, and the product and units, are confirmed after assessment.
questions: Which of the areas I am interested in suit treatment, and are any of my concerns not muscle-related?
Which product would you use, and why is that choice right for my areas?
What should I avoid before a flight or event, and how might bruising show in photos?

sections.title: How areas are mapped
sections.text: On the face, the physician may assess the forehead, around the eyes, between the brows, around the mouth and the jaw muscle. On the body, the trapezius and calves can be discussed. Several areas can be considered in one visit, but only suitable ones are treated.

sections.title: What the evidence covers
sections.text: Published research the clinic cites covers the jaw muscle only, in a small group, with a preparation and dose that do not convert to other products. It does not establish a universal dose or schedule, or results for other areas. Expectations are set individually.

sections.title: When another approach fits
sections.text: Fullness along the jaw that comes from fat rather than muscle may suit InMode instead. Concerns about lip or ear shape relate to filler rather than muscle relaxation. The physician explains which mechanism matches what you see in the mirror.

sections.title: Recovery and travel
sections.text: The injection itself is brief, usually within ten minutes. Temporary redness, small bumps at injection points or bruising can occur, varying by person and area. A fine needle is not an incision, but it does not guarantee an invisible recovery, so confirm timing before travel or events.

title: Potenza
intro: Potenza is a radiofrequency treatment for enlarged pores, uneven texture and laxity, delivered through surface-contact tips. After examining your skin, the physician chooses between the SFA, Diamond and DDR tips and sets the depth and settings.
questions: Are my scars shallow enough for Potenza, or do they need a staged plan with other methods?
How many sessions would a realistic course need, and can I complete it given my travel?
When can I wear makeup again, and how visible will marks be before an event or flight?

sections.title: What guides the plan
sections.text: The physician looks at pores, texture and laxity, and asks what bothers you most. Close-up daylight photos and your dates in Seoul help. Tip choice and shot count determine how much skin is covered and how many passes are made, so they are set for your area and concern.

sections.title: Why one session is rarely enough
sections.text: The energy is intended to stimulate collagen in the dermis, which takes time. Texture work is usually planned as a course spaced weeks apart, and how much changes varies. Deeper rolling or icepick scars usually need several methods rather than one device.

sections.title: Alternatives
sections.text: Acne Scar Revision stages several methods, including subcision, for deeper scars. Active breakouts may be better treated first with the Acne Care Package. Rejuran and Juvelook address skin quality through injection rather than energy. The physician assesses scar type before suggesting anything.

sections.title: Comfort and downtime
sections.text: Numbing cream is applied, but pressure, heat and some sharp passes are felt, often more along the jawline and hairline; settings can be adjusted. Redness, swelling and small tip marks are expected. Before leaving, makeup, sun care and event or flight timing are explained.

title: Radiesse
intro: Radiesse is a calcium hydroxylapatite injectable used two ways: at standard concentration to support the jawline and cheeks, or hyperdilute, spread thinly over loose, crepey skin. Structure where it sits is the first effect and collagen stimulation the intended second.
questions: Is my goal contour support or skin quality, and which preparation fits it?
Since Radiesse cannot be dissolved like hyaluronic-acid filler, how conservative should my first amount be?
How much swelling or bruising should I plan around before my flight?

sections.title: What the physician decides
sections.text: The assessment covers jawline and cheek contour, or looseness on the lower face and neck. The physician chooses the preparation and amount for your goal. Daylight photos from the front and side, and any filler you have had before, help with planning.

sections.title: Key limitation: reversibility
sections.text: Unlike hyaluronic-acid filler, Radiesse cannot be dissolved with an enzyme. That is why amount and placement are chosen carefully and a conservative first amount may be suggested. It is not used in the lips, and treatment is postponed during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

sections.title: Alternatives
sections.text: Hyaluronic-acid fillers, such as chin and lip filler, add volume where placed and can be dissolved. Juvelook is a PDLLA stimulator for skin or soft volume, and Rejuran targets skin quality. How much of each effect you notice, and for how long, varies by individual.

sections.title: Recovery and travel
sections.text: Swelling, bruising or tenderness can occur, and how long they remain visible varies by individual and injection area. Time in the room is usually short. Share travel and event dates so the plan leaves a sensible buffer before photos or flights.

title: Lip Filler
intro: Filler for lip volume, the lip border and the mouth corners. The physician looks at your lips at rest and while you talk, then agrees the product, amount and areas with you. Swelling and the degree of change vary.
questions: How much change can my lips carry without looking stretched or out of proportion with my face?
Would treating the mouth corners or border alone achieve what I want, rather than more volume?
Which warning signs after treatment mean I should contact the clinic the same day, even from abroad?

sections.title: How the plan is agreed
sections.text: Some people want a small change in volume, some more fullness, and some a cleaner border. The physician checks symmetry and movement, and may suggest a smaller amount first if your request would stretch the lip. Previous lip filler should be mentioned.

sections.title: Limits and duration
sections.text: Filler is gradually absorbed, and how long change stays visible varies with the product, the individual and how much the lips move. A maintenance rhythm is discussed rather than promised. Lips swell easily, so the immediate look is not the settled result.

sections.title: Related options
sections.text: Mouth corners can be included in the same plan if your anatomy suits it. Radiesse is not used in the lips. Chin shape, which affects how the lips sit in profile, is a separate filler decision, and muscle-related concerns are discussed with botulinum toxin.

sections.title: Aftercare, warning signs and travel
sections.text: For the first day or two, avoid alcohol, saunas and pressing the lips unless instructed. Contact the clinic straight away if the lip skin turns pale, dusky or blotchy, or pain worsens; these are uncommon but need same-day review. Plan photos and dinners around possible swelling.

title: Onda Lifting
intro: Onda uses microwave energy, branded Coolwaves, designed to concentrate in the fat layer under the skin while also warming the dermis. It is used for localized fat, cellulite and loose skin on the body, and for contour and laxity on the face.
questions: Is my concern localized fat, cellulite or loose skin, and is Onda the right device for that area?
How many sessions would you recommend, and does my stay allow a course?
Do any implants, devices or skin conditions rule Onda out for me?

sections.title: Assessment
sections.text: The physician examines the area to judge which concern dominates and whether it suits microwave energy. The energy amount is recommended based on the size of the area and what you want to change. A daylight photo of the area and your dates in Seoul help.

sections.title: What it is not
sections.text: Onda is not a weight-loss treatment and does not change body weight. The manufacturer describes target depths in the dermis and fat layer; that is design intent, and how much changes varies. A course is often recommended, with the number of sessions set after assessment.

sections.title: Alternatives
sections.text: InMode uses radiofrequency for chin fat and lower-face fullness, and InMode for the Body pairs radiofrequency with suction. Tuneliner Face combines ultrasound heat with micro-vibration for mild facial laxity. The physician tells you if your concern needs a different approach.

sections.title: Screening and recovery
sections.text: Tell the physician about a pacemaker, metal implants in the area, pregnancy or breastfeeding, or inflamed skin there. Warmth and discomfort are expected, and surface cooling does not make the session painless. Temporary redness, tenderness or mild swelling can follow, and recovery varies by area.

title: InMode
intro: Radiofrequency treatment for fat under the chin, a double chin and lower-face fullness. The physician chooses between the FX module, Forma RF and a fat-reduction step after judging whether the fullness is fat, loose skin or both.
questions: When you pinch and move my head, is my fullness fat, loose skin or both?
Would FX, Forma RF or a combination fit my concern, and what difference should I expect between them?
For how long should I avoid saunas, heavy drinking and hard exercise during my trip?

sections.title: The pinch test
sections.text: The physician checks the under-chin and jaw by pinching and with your head in different positions. If the fullness is not fat, InMode is unlikely to be the right choice, and you are told so. Suitable zones include the under-chin, jaw and lower cheeks.

sections.title: Limits
sections.text: Reduction of the heated fat layer is the intended effect, and how much occurs varies. Forma RF heats the skin itself as a stimulus for collagen remodelling, which is an intended response rather than an assured result. The clinic does not claim treatment of the SMAS layer.

sections.title: Alternatives
sections.text: A fat-dissolving injection is another option for a small, defined pocket under the chin. Onda and Tuneliner Face address contour and laxity with other energy types. If a square lower face comes from the jaw muscle, botulinum toxin may be discussed instead.

sections.title: Sensation and aftercare
sections.text: With FX, suction draws up a fold of skin and fat, so heat and pulling are expected; settings are adjusted if it becomes uncomfortable. Redness, warmth, tenderness or swelling can follow. Avoid heavy drinking, saunas and hard exercise for the period set, and use sunscreen outdoors.

title: Ear Filler
intro: Small amounts of filler placed at the helix, ear root and earlobe to add dimension, after the physician assesses the shape of your ear. The product, volume and how much dimension to add are confirmed at consultation.
questions: Given my ear shape, which points would you treat and how much dimension is sensible?
What is the plan if lumpiness or asymmetry appears after I return home?
Is a touch-up likely, and can it fit within my time in Seoul?

sections.title: Planning from your anatomy
sections.text: The design is planned against the anatomy of your ear from the start. A front photo with hair tied back and a side photo of each ear, plus your dates, let the clinic say whether filler is reasonable. The physician confirms product and volume in person.

sections.title: Risks are real
sections.text: No injection area is low risk, and the ear is not an exception. Swelling, bruising, lumpiness, infection and blockage of a blood vessel are possible. Assessment and technique reduce risk but do not remove it, and the physician reviews your history first.

sections.title: Sessions and alternatives
sections.text: Whether one session completes the plan depends on ear shape, product and how it settles; a touch-up is sometimes recommended. Filler elsewhere, such as the lips or chin, involves separate decisions. If filler is not a reasonable option for your ear, the clinic will say so.

sections.title: Comfort and recovery
sections.text: The ear is sensitive. Numbing cream or cooling is used first, and discomfort is mostly short and sharp at injection points; breaks can be requested. Temporary bruising, swelling or tenderness can occur, and the physician confirms what to plan for before travel.

title: Tune Re2O
intro: Tune Re2O is the clinic's collagen booster menu, which includes Elravie Re2O and Lateigen products, injected to support collagen and elastin in skin that has lost firmness. It aims at structure and skin quality rather than surface hydration.
questions: Which product in this collagen booster family suits my skin, and why that one?
Is my concern loss of firmness, or is it volume loss or deep sagging that a booster will not address?
How visible might injection marks be during my remaining days in Seoul?

sections.title: What is assessed
sections.text: The physician looks at loss of firmness and skin quality, then confirms the product and volume before anything is injected. Daylight photos without makeup and any boosters, filler or lifting treatments in the past year help decide whether a collagen booster is worth planning.

sections.title: Setting expectations
sections.text: Collagen stimulation is slow, so any change develops over weeks and depends on your starting skin. Supporting collagen and elastin is the aim, not a proven advantage over other products. Results are reviewed at follow-up and the plan adjusted from what is seen.

sections.title: Alternatives
sections.text: If lost volume or deep sagging is the main concern, a booster alone is unlikely to help, and volume or lifting treatments may be discussed. Rejuran and PDRN target skin quality by other mechanisms, and Juvelook is a PDLLA stimulator with skin and volume uses.

sections.title: Screening and recovery
sections.text: Tell the clinic about active skin infection, allergies to injectable products, blood thinners, pregnancy or breastfeeding. Small injection marks, redness, swelling or bruising can appear, and how long they last varies. Discuss work, events and flights before choosing the date.

title: Tuneliner Face
intro: Tuneliner Face is a non-invasive treatment that delivers focused ultrasound heat and physical micro-vibration through one handpiece, for mild laxity and a softening facial contour. The physician examines your face to confirm whether it fits and how many sessions make sense.
questions: Is my laxity mild enough for Tuneliner Face, or does it call for a different approach?
If I can only visit once, is a single session still worthwhile for me?
How might warmth or redness affect my plans on the day of treatment?

sections.title: Who it suits
sections.text: The consultation focus is mild laxity and an early softening of contour. Heavy sagging usually needs a different approach. Recent lifting treatments, daylight photos from the front and sides, and how many visits you can make in Seoul all shape the recommendation.

sections.title: What the device does and does not claim
sections.text: Heat is directed at deeper layers where collagen remodelling and tissue contraction are the intended responses, with vibration applied at the same time. The clinic does not claim the combination lifts more than heat alone, and responses vary.

sections.title: Alternatives
sections.text: Shurink delivers focused ultrasound at set depths, including the SMAS layer. InMode addresses fullness from fat under the chin, and Onda uses microwave energy for contour and laxity. If another treatment fits better, the physician explains why at consultation.

sections.title: Comfort, recovery and timing
sections.text: There are no needles or incisions, but heat and some discomfort are felt. Visible recovery is often limited, yet temporary redness, warmth, swelling or tenderness can occur. Active acne, dermatitis or infection, pregnancy or breastfeeding are reasons to wait.

title: Oligio Thermal RF Lifting
intro: Oligio is a monopolar radiofrequency device that heats a broad column of dermis on the face and around the eyes, with collagen remodelling over months as the intended response. It is not designed to reach the deeper SMAS plane.
questions: Is the change I see coming from the skin layer, or from deeper tissue that Oligio will not reach?
Why would you choose Oligio over Thermage for me, apart from price?
Should I treat my face, my eyes or both, and how would that affect comfort and recovery?

sections.title: Is a dermal device the right tool?
sections.text: The physician assesses where the laxity sits and whether a dermal treatment fits. Crepey texture and early laxity on the face and around the eyes are the usual focus. If most of the change comes from deeper tissue, you hear that before booking.

sections.title: Comparing with Thermage
sections.text: Both are monopolar radiofrequency devices from different makers. A different price does not make them the same treatment, and does not make either work better. Oligio spreads energy over wide zones at moderate depth, which is a different delivery pattern, not a superior one.

sections.title: Limits and other routes
sections.text: How much remodelling develops varies, and duration cannot be promised; repeats are decided at follow-up. The study cited by Tune Clinic concerns monopolar radiofrequency as a class and does not establish results for Oligio or an individual treatment plan. For deeper sagging, Ultherapy, Shurink or threads may be discussed.

sections.title: Screening and recovery
sections.text: A pacemaker or implanted electrical device, metal implants in the area, active skin infection, pregnancy or breastfeeding can rule it out. Each pulse can feel hot despite cooling and vibration, and pauses are possible. Redness, warmth or mild swelling can follow.

title: Chin Filler
intro: Hyaluronic-acid filler placed at the chin to add projection or length and to smooth the line between the lower lip and chin. The physician decides in person whether the chin, the jawline or neither is the right place to work.
questions: Is my chin set back or short for my face, or is my concern actually fat or loose skin along the jaw?
How will you check my profile during treatment so the shape suits my face?
If I change my mind or the shape is uneven after I return home, how would dissolving it be arranged?

sections.title: Who it suits
sections.text: Chin filler suits a chin that sits back or is short for the face, or a lip-to-chin line that folds inward. The physician marks the chin with you sitting up and places filler in small amounts, checking the profile between passes, so you see the shape before leaving.

sections.title: Who should look elsewhere
sections.text: A double chin or loose skin along the jaw is usually a fat or laxity problem, and the physician will not add volume where it will not help. For those concerns, InMode, a fat-dissolving injection or a lifting treatment may be more relevant.

sections.title: Duration and reversibility
sections.text: Hyaluronic-acid filler is absorbed over time, at a rate that varies by product, amount and individual. The chin moves less than the lips, but no duration is guaranteed. Unlike Radiesse, it can be dissolved if you change your mind.

sections.title: Risks and flying home
sections.text: Swelling, bruising, lumpiness, asymmetry, infection and, rarely, blockage of a blood vessel are possible. Most people return to normal activity the same day, and swelling or bruising is usually most visible in the first few days. Mention a short stay so treatment is planned around your flight.

title: Sagging jawline and cheeks
intro: A blurred jawline and lower cheeks usually reflect two separate changes: skin that recoils less because dermal collagen and elastin have thinned, and deeper fat and connective tissue that have descended. They look alike in a mirror but are assessed and treated differently.
questions: In my face, is laxity of the skin or descent of deeper tissue doing more of the work?
Which layer would each treatment you suggest act on, and why does that match my anatomy?
How much time between treatment and flying home should I plan for the option you recommend?

sections.title: How the physician tells them apart
sections.text: Most faces have both changes in different proportions, and that proportion steers the plan. The same photograph can show mostly laxity in one person and mostly descent in another, so a plan built from a photo alone is unreliable. The deciding examination is done in person.

sections.title: Matching the tool to the layer
sections.text: Radiofrequency devices such as Thermage and Oligio heat the dermis. Focused ultrasound such as Ultherapy reaches set depths including the SMAS. Thread lifting physically repositions tissue. Each acts in a different place, so the recommendation depends on where your change sits.

sections.title: Limits to accept
sections.text: These non-surgical treatments are aimed at early to moderate change. Heavy sagging or a large amount of excess skin is outside what energy devices are designed for, and threads have their own limits. Where hollowing is part of the picture, volume loss is a separate question.

sections.title: If the advice differs from your plan
sections.text: The physician may recommend something other than what you came for, and will explain the reasoning and tradeoffs. Nothing is done without informed consent, and deciding to think further or go elsewhere is a reasonable outcome. Recovery and travel buffers vary by treatment.

title: Pigmentation, melasma, and dark spots
intro: Brown marks differ in where the pigment sits. Sharply bordered freckles and sun spots usually lie near the surface, while melasma forms broader, hazy patches in which pigment often sits at more than one depth and responds strongly to sun and heat.
questions: Are my marks sharply bordered spots, melasma, or a mix, and how does that change the plan?
What role will daily sun protection play, and what happens if I tan during or after treatment?
Could any laser step darken my pigment, and how would that be managed once I am home?

sections.title: Why the type matters
sections.text: Pigment cells in the lower epidermis produce more melanin when triggered by ultraviolet light, heat, inflammation after acne or a procedure, or hormonal change. Where the excess settles decides how a mark looks and behaves, which is why two similar photos can need different plans.

sections.title: Managed, not erased
sections.text: Melasma is described as managed rather than removed. It can darken if treated too hard and can return, so gentle settings over several sessions with daily sun protection are part of the approach. Sharper surface spots behave differently and are assessed separately.

sections.title: Starting points
sections.text: The First Pigment laser Omakase combines three laser steps in one first visit. Enlighten pigment treatment uses two wavelengths chosen for surface or deeper pigment. Marks left by active acne may settle better once breakouts are controlled, so acne care can come first.

sections.title: Before you decide
sections.text: The physician may suggest something different from what you asked for, and will explain why. A recent tan can mean laser is adjusted or postponed. Redness is common afterwards, and treated spots may darken before fading, so confirm a travel buffer at consultation.

title: Acne scars and post-acne marks
intro: Acne leaves two kinds of mark that are easy to confuse. Flat brown or red discolouration is pigment or dilated vessels with an unchanged surface, and usually fades over months. A scar is a change in contour where collagen was destroyed, and it does not resolve on its own.
questions: Which of my marks are flat discolouration and which are true scars?
Which scar types do I have in each zone of my face, and how would the approach differ between them?
Is my acne controlled enough to start scar work, and how many trips might a staged plan take?

sections.title: Recognising scar types
sections.text: Atrophic scars are usually described by shape. Icepick scars are narrow and deep, boxcar scars are wider with defined edges, and rolling scars are shallow undulations tethered from underneath. Most faces carry a mixture, and different zones may need different methods.

sections.title: Why the plan follows the examination
sections.text: A photograph or a single label does not capture the mix. The physician looks at the skin, often under side lighting, before building a plan. Active breakouts usually need control first, since new inflammation can leave new marks.

sections.title: Options that may be combined
sections.text: Acne Scar Revision stages methods such as subcision with a collagen stimulator, with laser or radiofrequency microneedling added only if needed. Potenza may form part of a plan for shallow scarring and texture. Flat discolouration is a pigment question rather than a scar question.

sections.title: Realistic expectations and downtime
sections.text: Treatment may make scars less noticeable over several sessions. Improvement varies, and scars are not erased. Downtime varies by method and can include redness, swelling, bruising or peeling. If the physician recommends something different from what you expected, the reasoning is explained and nothing proceeds without consent.

title: Volume loss
intro: With age, elasticity fades and the cheeks drop and hollow at the sides. The face can then read broader, heavier and more tired, even though overall volume has decreased. Separating hollowing from sagging is the first step.
questions: Is the tired look in my face mainly from hollowing, from sagging, or both?
Would repositioning tissue be enough, or would I also need a separate volume treatment?
How much recovery time would the plan you suggest need before I fly home?

sections.title: What the physician looks at
sections.text: The assessment considers where the cheek has dropped, how thin the skin is, and whether true hollowing is present. These change what is suggested, because a lifting treatment does not replace volume and a volume treatment does not lift sagging tissue.

sections.title: Treatment directions
sections.text: Thread lifting repositions sagging tissue, and Cheek Hollow Lifting applies threads to cheeks that look hollow at the sides. Where real volume loss contributes, a volume treatment may be discussed separately. The proportion of each problem decides the mix.

sections.title: Limitations
sections.text: A broader, heavier look can come from sagging rather than excess volume, so adding filler is not automatically the answer. Very heavy skin excess may not suit threads. How much any treatment changes, and for how long, varies by individual.

sections.title: Before agreeing to a plan
sections.text: The physician may recommend something other than what you expected and will explain the tradeoffs. Nothing is done without informed consent. Swelling, bruising and tightness are common after threads, so treatment early in your trip leaves time before the flight home.

title: Enlarged pores
intro: Pores around the nose and cheeks can look enlarged in close-up photos or under makeup. A pore is the opening of a hair follicle and its oil gland, and what changes over time is how visible it is, not how many there are.
questions: Is my pore visibility driven mostly by oil output, by loss of skin elasticity, or by both?
Which treatment would you suggest, and how much visible recovery does it involve?
How should I take baseline photos so that any change can be judged fairly?

sections.title: What makes pores look larger
sections.text: Size is set largely by genetics and oil production. Higher oil output widens the opening; sun and age reduce the elasticity holding it, so it springs back less; and a wider opening collects shadow. Lighting and season change how pores look, so a single photo is a poor baseline.

sections.title: What treatment can change
sections.text: Pores are not closed permanently, and their number does not change. What can change is oil output, the condition and thickness of the surrounding skin, and how much shadow the opening collects. Expectations are set around visibility, not disappearance.

sections.title: Treatment directions
sections.text: Radiofrequency treatment such as Potenza targets texture and pores over a course. Oil-related concerns overlap with acne care, which is aimed at the sebaceous glands. Where laxity contributes, tightening options may be discussed. The physician matches the approach to the cause.

sections.title: Recovery depends on the treatment
sections.text: Downtime depends on the treatment, not the concern. Options range from sessions with no visible recovery to sessions with a few days of redness or flaking. The physician confirms expected recovery for your plan before you book, and explains any recommendation that differs from your request.

title: Acne Scar Revision
intro: Staged treatment for rolling, boxcar and icepick acne scars. The starting program combines a Juvelook skin booster with subcision, which uses a needle under the skin to release the bands that pull rolling scars down. Other methods are added only if your scars call for them.
questions: Which of my scars are rolling, boxcar or icepick, and which methods would each need?
How many sessions do you expect, and how far apart, given that I am travelling?
How long might bruising from subcision stay visible before my flight?

sections.title: Examination under side lighting
sections.text: The physician sorts scars by type and checks whether acne is still active; scar work usually waits until breakouts are under control. Cold sores, keloid scarring, recent isotretinoin or an active skin infection can mean a method is postponed or left out.

sections.title: What the starting program covers
sections.text: The starting program is a Juvelook skin booster with subcision. Fractional laser, radiofrequency microneedling and focal TCA are separate options, added only when the scars call for them. Final components and the quote are confirmed at the in-person consultation.

sections.title: Steps, not erasure
sections.text: Several sessions spaced weeks apart are usual, so the skin can heal in between. The number depends on scar types and response. Treatment may make scars less noticeable over several sessions. Improvement varies, and scars are not erased. Flat brown or red marks are a separate pigment question.

sections.title: Downtime and travel buffer
sections.text: Subcision is done through small needle entry points after numbing, so bruising and swelling over treated scars are expected for several days. Depending on the methods used, redness or peeling can last from a few days to about a week. Confirm a buffer before flying.

title: Alltite
intro: Alltite is a radiofrequency skin-tightening device for early laxity along the jawline, jowls and lower face. The handpiece heats the deeper skin in overlapping passes while the surface temperature is watched. Areas and shot count are set after examination.
questions: Is my laxity early enough for radiofrequency tightening, or too advanced for it to be reasonable?
How much area would the starting option cover, and would my areas need a larger plan?
How sensitive am I likely to be to the heat, and is numbing worth arranging?

sections.title: Assessment
sections.text: The physician looks at your face at rest and in profile and checks the skin along the jaw and cheeks. How much laxity there is, where it sits and how you tolerate heat are the deciding factors. If laxity is too advanced, you are told before anything is booked.

sections.title: Limits
sections.text: Radiofrequency heats the skin across a broad area and is aimed at early laxity, not heavy sagging. The starting option covers a limited area, so larger areas need a larger plan, confirmed after assessment. Response varies by individual.

sections.title: Alternatives
sections.text: HIFU devices such as Shurink focus ultrasound at set depths under the skin, while Thermage and Oligio are other radiofrequency options. Neither type suits everyone; skin thickness and where the laxity sits decide it, and the physician says if another device makes more sense.

sections.title: Comfort and recovery
sections.text: Most people feel deep warmth. The physician lowers the energy if it becomes uncomfortable, and numbing can be arranged. Redness and warmth are common afterwards and usually settle the same day, but recovery varies, so confirm aftercare and a travel buffer.

title: Cheek Hollow Lifting
intro: Thread lifting for cheeks that have started to sag and look hollow at the sides. It is not filler. The physician assesses skin thickness and where the sagging sits, then chooses the thread type, count and direction.
questions: How much of my hollow look is sagging that threads can reposition, and how much is real volume loss?
Is my skin thick enough for threads, and would the plan differ between my two sides?
How long might tightness when opening my mouth last, and will it affect eating or talking on my trip?

sections.title: Zone-by-zone examination
sections.text: With you sitting upright, the physician looks at where the cheek has dropped zone by zone and checks skin thickness and elasticity. Thin skin, heavy tissue and differences between sides each change the choice, and the plan is marked on your face rather than taken from a template.

sections.title: When threads alone are not enough
sections.text: If part of the hollow look is volume loss rather than sagging, threads will not fill it, and a volume treatment may be discussed separately. Sometimes threads are not the right answer at all, and the physician will say so.

sections.title: Related approaches
sections.text: General thread lifting addresses sagging in the mid-face, jawline and under the chin. Energy-based lifting may suit earlier looseness without much descent. Your skin is recorded before treatment and at follow-up so change can be judged against your own baseline.

sections.title: Risks and recovery
sections.text: Swelling, bruising, tightness and tenderness when opening the mouth wide can occur. Less common problems include small dimples at entry points, asymmetry, a thread that can be felt or seen, and infection. Aftercare covers washing, makeup, exercise and facial massage; confirm a buffer before travel.

title: CoolSoniq
intro: CoolSoniq is a focused ultrasound lifting device with an applicator that cools the skin surface during each pass. It is used for early laxity along the jawline, lower face and brow, with areas and depths marked by the physician at consultation.
questions: Which areas and depths would you mark on my face, especially where the skin is thin or over bone?
How does my previous experience with HIFU change your plan or settings?
Is flying home on the same day as treatment reasonable for me?

sections.title: Assessment
sections.text: The physician assesses where the skin has loosened and how thick it is, then marks areas and depths. Areas over bone and areas of thin skin receive different settings. Mention any previous HIFU and how you tolerated it, since that shapes the plan.

sections.title: Limits
sections.text: Focused ultrasound is aimed at early laxity rather than heavy sagging. Cooling the surface supports comfort but does not remove risk. The shot count for your areas is confirmed after assessment, and response varies by individual.

sections.title: Comparable devices
sections.text: Ultherapy and Shurink also deliver focused ultrasound at set depths. Thermage uses monopolar radiofrequency to warm the dermis instead. The choice depends on where the looseness sits and how your skin has responded before, rather than on the device name.

sections.title: Comfort, recovery and travel
sections.text: Deep heat or brief prickling can be felt, especially over bone, and settings can be adjusted. Redness, mild swelling or tenderness along the jaw can occur, and occasionally small bruises. Normal activity is usually possible the same day; tell the physician your flight time beforehand.

title: Enlighten
intro: Pigment laser treatment with the Cutera Enlighten, which uses a 532nm wavelength for surface pigment and a 1,064nm wavelength for deeper pigment. Listed as Pigmentation Deep Treatment, it is separate from The First Pigment laser Omakase.
questions: Is my pigment freckles, sun spots, melasma or deeper acquired pigment, and how deep does it sit?
If melasma is present, how gentle will the settings be and how many sessions should I expect?
Have I tanned recently enough that treatment should wait?

sections.title: Identifying the pigment first
sections.text: Pigment is not one condition. Freckles and sun spots sit near the surface, while melasma and some acquired pigment sit deeper and react to heat. The physician checks type, depth, spread, skin sensitivity and recent tanning before choosing a wavelength and settings area by area.

sections.title: The melasma caveat
sections.text: Melasma can darken if treated too hard, and it can return. It is treated at gentle settings over several sessions, with daily sun protection as part of the plan. A single session is not presented as clearing pigment.

sections.title: Choosing between pigment options
sections.text: The First Pigment laser Omakase is a combined introductory program with three laser steps and a consultation. Enlighten is a single-device pigment treatment. Acne-related marks may call for acne control first. The physician suggests which suits your pigment.

sections.title: Recovery
sections.text: Mild redness or tightness can occur, and surface spots can darken and flake before they fade. Recovery varies by individual and by pigment type. Sun protection afterwards matters, so plan outdoor time and travel with this in mind.

title: Fat-Dissolving Injection
intro: An injection for a small, defined pocket of fat, such as a double chin, fullness along the jawline or a small area on the body. The aim is a local change in contour in people at or near a stable weight, not weight loss.
questions: Is my fullness fat that is likely to respond, or loose skin or muscle that will not change?
How many sessions might my area need, and can they fit around my visits to Seoul?
How noticeable will under-chin swelling be in the first days, and should I avoid events then?

sections.title: Is it really fat?
sections.text: Loose skin and muscle can look like fat but will not change with injection. The physician checks this first, along with whether the area is small enough. Sometimes an energy-based contouring device is the more sensible option, and you will be told.

sections.title: Limits
sections.text: It will not change your overall weight. More than one session is usually needed, with the number depending on the area and how it responds. Individual results vary, and the published scope covers one area per session, not a full-body plan.

sections.title: Alternatives
sections.text: InMode uses radiofrequency for fat under the chin and lower-face fullness, and InMode for the Body treats body areas with radiofrequency and suction. Where the concern is a missing curve rather than excess fat, body filler addresses the opposite problem.

sections.title: What recovery feels like
sections.text: Numbing is applied, but stinging or burning after injection is common. Swelling, tenderness, firmness and occasional bruising follow, and under-chin swelling can be obvious for the first day or two. Plan event and flight dates with this in mind.

title: IV Therapy & Drips
intro: Physician-supervised intravenous drips, with the formulation chosen by the physician after a short medical check of your goals, allergies, medications and health conditions. Whether a drip is appropriate is decided after medical assessment; it does not treat disease.
questions: Given my medications and health history, is a drip advisable for me today at all?
Which formulation would you choose for my goal, and what does it contain?
If I am booking other treatments, in what order and on which day should the drip go?

sections.title: The medical check
sections.text: Before anything is started, tell the physician about allergies, regular medications, pregnancy or breastfeeding, and health conditions. You do not need to choose a blend in advance. After the check, the physician recommends a formulation, or advises against a drip that day.

sections.title: What a drip is not
sections.text: A drip does not treat jet lag or illness, and it does not replace drinking water and rest. Some patients ask about one around a long flight; whether that suits you is a medical decision. The final formulation is confirmed individually.

sections.title: Combining with other treatments
sections.text: A drip can be booked on the same day as another treatment if the physician agrees after looking at your full plan. Mention every treatment you are booking so the order and timing can be checked.

sections.title: During and after
sections.text: A needle is placed in a vein and you rest in a chair while the drip runs, usually for under an hour depending on the formulation. A small bruise can appear at the needle site. Tell the physician what you have planned for the rest of the day.

title: Laser Hair Removal
intro: Laser hair reduction for the face and body. The physician assesses your skin tone and hair, then sets the wavelength, settings and areas. Hair reduces over a course of sessions spaced weeks apart, and maintenance may be needed.
questions: Will my hair colour and skin tone respond well, and what precautions apply to my settings?
How many sessions does my area likely need, and can I continue the course at home?
Do my current medications or a recent tan mean I should wait?

sections.title: What decides suitability
sections.text: Very light, grey or red hair responds poorly to laser in general, and darker skin needs carefully chosen settings. A fresh tan, light-sensitising medication, pregnancy, or a rash, infection or cold sore in the area can mean changing settings or waiting.

sections.title: Why it takes a course
sections.text: Hair grows in cycles, and the laser acts on hairs actively growing at the time. Reduction therefore builds over repeated sessions, and maintenance may be needed. It is described as hair reduction rather than permanent removal.

sections.title: Planning around a short trip
sections.text: A single visit can start a course but will not finish one. If you can return to Seoul, or continue with a clinic at home, tell the physician so the first session is planned accordingly. Shaving between sessions is fine; waxing and plucking remove the root the laser needs.

sections.title: After the session
sections.text: Redness and small bumps around the follicles can appear straight after, and how long they last varies. Keep the area out of the sun as part of aftercare. Areas assessed include the upper lip and chin, underarms, arms, legs and body lines.

title: Neck Wrinkle Filler
intro: Small amounts of fine hyaluronic-acid filler, The Chaeum, placed into horizontal neck creases, with a PDRN injection in the same visit. The realistic aim is softer-looking creases, not a line-free neck.
questions: Are my neck lines creases that filler can soften, or loose or crepey skin that needs a different approach?
Which warning signs of a blocked blood vessel should I watch for after leaving, and how do I reach the clinic?
How visible might bumps or marks along the lines be while I am still travelling?

sections.title: Is filler right for your neck?
sections.text: The physician examines the lines, explains what filler can and cannot do, and confirms suitability. When neck skin is loose and hanging rather than creased, filler is unlikely to help much. A daylight photo with your chin level and your dates help the clinic advise before you travel.

sections.title: Limits
sections.text: Filler can soften how deep a crease looks, but horizontal neck lines rarely go away completely. The filler is gradually absorbed, and how long the effect lasts varies with product, individual and neck movement. Maintenance is discussed rather than promised.

sections.title: Alternatives
sections.text: Fine crepey skin across the whole neck may call for skin treatments instead, such as polynucleotide or PDRN injections. Hyperdilute Radiesse is used with the intent of stimulating collagen in crepey or loose neck skin. The physician explains which option suits your lines.

sections.title: Risks and recovery
sections.text: The neck is delicate, so small, measured amounts are used. Guidance on hyaluronic-acid filler stresses prompt recognition and treatment of a blocked blood vessel, and no injection area is described as safe. Small bumps, marks, swelling or bruising along the lines can follow.

title: PDRN Salmon Injection
intro: PDRN (polydeoxyribonucleotide) injections use DNA fragments purified from salmon and are aimed at tired, damaged or sensitive skin. The physician decides at the in-person consultation whether PDRN suits your skin and how much to use.
questions: Is PDRN or a polynucleotide product like Rejuran more suitable for my skin, and what is the difference?
How many sessions would you plan, and how far apart, given my travel?
When can I wash my face, wear makeup and exercise again?

sections.title: What it is assessed for
sections.text: Concerns assessed for PDRN include fine lines, loss of elasticity, enlarged pores, rough texture, acne scars and redness. Suitability is decided individually. Daylight photos without makeup, what bothers you, and your dates in Seoul help the physician give an initial view.

sections.title: Limits
sections.text: PDRN is often planned as more than one session, but the number and spacing are set by the physician and reviewed as you go. It is aimed at skin quality, and how much changes varies by individual.

sections.title: Alternatives
sections.text: Rejuran is a salmon-derived polynucleotide, and polynucleotide and PDRN products are not interchangeable. Juvelook and Tune Re2O are collagen-stimulating injectables. Each targets skin quality differently, and the physician explains which formulation suits your concern.

sections.title: Screening and recovery
sections.text: Tell the physician about a fish or salmon allergy, pregnancy or breastfeeding, or an active skin infection in the area. Numbing cream can be used. Redness, swelling or small bumps at injection points may occur. Moisturising and sun protection are part of aftercare.

title: Skin Care & Management
intro: Esthetician-led cleansing, hydration and calming care inside a physician-led clinic, timed around any procedure you are having. Sessions support medical treatment rather than replace it, and the physician's plan decides when a session fits.
questions: Is a care session appropriate on the same day as my procedure, or should my skin be left alone?
Which care option suits my skin type and recent treatments?
If I have an event or flight the same day, which gentler steps would you choose?

sections.title: Who it suits
sections.text: The usual focus is dry, reactive or recently treated skin, and upkeep between procedures. The esthetician looks at your skin and asks about recent treatments before starting with gentle cleansing. Options include ion or LED care, LDM, blackhead care or bridal mask care.

sections.title: Care, not a medical treatment
sections.text: Sessions are esthetician-led, with the physician responsible for the overall plan. They support medical treatment and are not a substitute for it. If your concern needs a medical procedure, that decision belongs to the physician.

sections.title: Timing with procedures
sections.text: After some lasers or injections the skin should be left alone for a while, while after others a calming session is reasonable. Whether a session goes on the same day is confirmed when your plan is made, following the physician's aftercare.

sections.title: Possible redness and travel
sections.text: Some people go a little pink after cleansing or blackhead care, varying with skin and session. Mention allergies to skincare products. Share travel dates and any procedure you are booking so the clinic can suggest which session to book and when.
